findings.description: Rejecting a proposed replacement leaves the original decision's supersede_proposed_by pointing to that rejected row. This guard then refuses every subsequent agent replacement proposal.
findings.failure_mode: After an agent proposes B to supersede decided row A and the operator rejects B, A remains decided but cannot receive another agent replacement proposal without manual repair or an operator override.
findings.suggested_fix: When rejecting a replacement, clear the original row's matching supersede_proposed_by atomically, or make this guard block only replacements that remain proposed.

findings.description: Import locks only the destination ledger, snapshots the pending file, and later deletes that source without coordinating with its writers.
findings.failure_mode: A worktree writer can successfully append a pending row after import reads the source but before this deletion. Import commits only its earlier snapshot, then deletes the newly appended row without importing it.
findings.suggested_fix: Coordinate import and pending writes through a shared source lock held through source removal. Ensure the lock identity is shared across the main checkout and linked worktrees.

findings.description: `ctx_signals` emits a non-live `prd prd-status:` signal whenever grimoires/loa/prd.md has a `**Status**` line containing 'autonomous' or 'unattended'. `is_unattended` treats that signal exactly like a live run signal. `op_confirm` deliberately only refuses on `live_run_signal`, so it proceeds under a PRD signal, but it then calls `derive_attribution 0`, whose first branch (`if is_unattended`) discards `--answer-ref` with a WARN and leaves REF empty. The confirm jq then sets `.decided_by = (if decided_by_ref tests OPREF then "operator" else .proposed_by end)`, which resolves to the agent voice. The same `is_unattended` check also makes `op_reject` die on a decided row ('context is unattended') and makes `op_supersede` by the operator fall into the agent path (sets `supersede_proposed_by` instead of superseding). The /decisions command doc states the cli ref 'is what records decided_by: operator', so this is a spec violation that persists for the whole project lifetime once the PRD status mentions autonomy.
findings.failure_mode: An operator typing `/decisions confirm --id DEC-0007` in an interactive session with a PRD marked autonomous gets a ledger row with `status: decided`, `decided_by: agent`, no operator ref, and `transitions[].by: operator:decisions-command`. The `list --not-decided-by operator` SDD appendix then keeps reporting the row as an agent decision after the operator approved it, and `reject` on decided rows is permanently refused.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the signal kinds: in `derive_attribution`, only drop `--answer-ref`/`--as` when `live_run_signal` is true (or when the caller is not `is_operator_call`), and use `live_run_signal` instead of `is_unattended` in the operator branches of `op_reject` and `op_supersede`. Keep `is_unattended` (live + prd) only for deciding the landing status in `op_new`. Add a bats case: PRD with `**Status:** Autonomous`, interactive env, confirm with a cli ref, assert `decided_by == operator`.

findings.description: The pending file is created with `cat > "$TARGET"` inside `resolve_target write`, which runs before `acquire_lock`. Two concurrent worktree writers (e.g. parallel sprint tasks both told to run `dec-write-lib.sh new`) can both observe `! -f $TARGET`; the slower one's `cat >` can truncate the file after the faster one has already locked, appended a row and swapped it in.
findings.failure_mode: A PEND row written by the first process is silently overwritten by the empty `decisions: []` header from the second process; no error is raised and the row is lost before import.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the header creation after `acquire_lock "$TARGET"` (lock on the intended path even when it does not exist yet, which `lock_path` already supports since it hashes the path), and re-check `-f` under the lock before writing the header.

findings.description: `op_import` locks only the live ledger (`acquire_lock "$TARGET"`), never the pending file it consumes, and `lock_path` keys locks under this checkout's `.run`, while a worktree writer locks the same pending file under the worktree's `.run`. After `verify_and_swap`, the import unconditionally runs `rm -f -- "$from"`. A worktree process that appends a row between the import's `read_ledger "$from"` and the `rm -f` loses that row.
findings.failure_mode: A PEND row appended during an in-flight import is deleted with the pending file and never reaches the live ledger; the import output lists only the rows read earlier.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-read `$from` after `verify_and_swap` and refuse to delete it if its row count or ids differ from what was imported (print the leftover ids instead), or lock the pending file too using a lock path derived from the pending file's own directory so both checkouts contend on the same lock.

findings.cross_file_justification: decisions.md (in diff) claims the operator-only guarantee rests on `disable-model-invocation: true` plus a static test that no other command calls these operations; the runtime guard in dec-write-lib.sh (in diff) is only a string comparison on `--recorded-by`.
findings.description: `disable-model-invocation` only prevents the model from invoking the `/decisions` slash command through the Skill tool. Nothing stops a model running Bash (the normal state in every other skill) from executing `dec-write-lib.sh confirm --id DEC-0007 --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:... --answer-ref cli:...` directly, which the lib accepts as an operator call and records `decided_by: operator`. The static bats grep catches committed skill text, not ad-hoc tool calls.
findings.failure_mode: An agent in an unattended run (or one that was prompt-injected via untrusted ledger text) can self-confirm its proposed rows and attribute them to the operator, defeating the ledger's purpose; the audit trail shows a normal operator confirmation.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat this as a documented limitation or add a runtime check that an agent cannot forge from Bash, e.g. require confirm/reject-decided/supersede/context --clear to run with a TTY on stdin (`[[ -t 0 ]]`) or with an operator-held token from outside the repo/env the agent controls; at minimum state the actual trust boundary in decisions.md instead of 'the model cannot invoke it'.

findings.cross_file_justification: autonomous-agent/SKILL.md (in diff) now instructs runs to call `context --set-unattended`; the marker that creates is fresh for the full TTL in the same session, and op_confirm (in diff) refuses on any fresh marker.
findings.description: `context --set-unattended` stamps the marker with the current session id, and `marker_state` reports it `fresh` for `unattended_marker_ttl_hours` (default 24) as long as the session id matches or is unset. After the autonomous run finishes, the operator in that same session typing `/decisions confirm` is refused for up to 24 hours. decisions.md documents `clear-unattended` only 'when the session-start surface reports it stale', and the surface hook only emits a notice for stale markers, so the operator gets no guidance on how to proceed.
findings.failure_mode: Operator confirmation is blocked for the rest of the day after any autonomous run in the same session; the refusal text says 'confirm after the run, interactively' with no repair step, and the documented repair path (`clear-unattended`) is described as applying only to stale markers.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the run-mode completion/halt path clear or expire the marker (e.g. write `completed_at` and treat it as stale), or include 'run `/decisions clear-unattended` if the run has finished' in the confirm refusal message and in decisions.md, and have the surface hook mention fresh markers too.
